title: U-lock a bike wheel to a stand: shackle through the spokes and round the post, crossbar onto both legs at once
instruction: Lock the bike's back wheel to the bike stand with the U-lock.
context: Locking a bike to a street stand is an everyday job; here a parent locks a real child's bike (12-inch wheels) to a full-size stand with a full-size U-lock. The lock only holds the wheel if its shackle goes round the rim itself (one leg between two spokes, the other outside the tyre) and round the stand's tube, and the loose crossbar is pushed fully home on both leg ends at once. None of this is stated: a lock round the stand but not the rim, or the wheel but not the stand, leaves the wheel free to take, and a crossbar not pushed home does not lock. The stand's leg is 8 mm from the tyre, so the rigid shackle must be carried level and threaded through a 25 mm gap between spokes while the other hand brings the crossbar round behind the wheel. Unlike the padlock lockout tasks on the board (a hinged shackle snapped shut through one hole), refitting a quick-release wheel or loading a bike on a bus rack (seating it in a fixture), two loose rigid parts are joined round two fixed objects.
setup: The table top stands for the pavement. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Bike: a child's bike with 12-inch wheels (ISO 203 rims, 57-203 tyres, 31.7 cm across; 16 radial 2 mm steel spokes per wheel, aluminium rim 17-20 cm across), red steel frame, standing on its kickstand; its frame and front wheel are fixed in place. Its wheelbase is 48 cm, shorter than the 58 to 60 cm of real 12-inch bikes, so that the whole bike fits on the table; the wheels and tyres are true size. It faces away from the robot to the left: its back hub is at x 38, y -1, 15.9 cm up, its front hub at x 58.3, y 42.5. The back wheel turns freely on its axle (0.8 kg, light bearing drag); at the start two spokes sit 11.25 degrees above and below the horizontal line from the hub toward the back of the bike. Stand: a fixed, full-size Sheffield cycle stand of 48 mm galvanised steel tube, 75 cm tall, standing on the table top, legs 70 cm apart (commercial stands are about 75 to 100 cm long), standing parallel to the bike between it and the robot; one leg is at x 26.5, y -11.3, 8 mm in front of the back tyre and 14.2 cm from the hub along the bike, the other at x 56.1, y 52.1. U-lock (the size and mass of a common standard 4 x 9 inch U-lock such as a Kryptonite KryptoLok Standard: inside 10.2 x 22.9 cm, 12.7 mm hardened steel shackle, 1.32 kg in all), lying flat in two parts. Shackle: 0.62 kg, a vinyl sleeve 20 mm across over the bend and the first 7 cm of each leg, the rest bare steel; it lies with its bend toward the robot at x 13, y 17 (centre of the bend), legs pointing away from the robot parallel to the bike. Crossbar: 0.70 kg, black steel, 30 x 30 mm, 16 cm long with a 5 cm lock head at its right end; two 17 x 17 mm sockets, 20 mm deep and 11.5 cm apart, open toward the robot; it lies parallel to the bike with the midpoint between its sockets at x 25, y -30. The crossbar locks when pushed onto both leg ends until they are within 4 mm of the socket bottoms (16 mm in) and within 4 mm of the sockets' centre lines; it fits either way round and, once locked, stays on. No key is used. Fixed layout, no randomisation.
scoring: Read at the end, from a photo and by hand. The lock goes round the rim if the rim passes through the closed lock (the shackle and the line across its leg ends): the wheel cannot be turned or lifted out of it. It goes round the stand if the stand's leg or top bar passes through it. Locked: the crossbar is on both leg ends and has caught (both ends at least 16 mm into its sockets and within 4 mm of the sockets' centre lines); once caught it stays on, as a real crossbar does without its key. 1.0: locked, round both the rim and the stand, every finger of both grippers at least 3 cm from both lock parts and both parts moving less than 2 mm over the last second, held for 1 s. 0.5: the same lock, correctly closed round both the rim and the stand, but a gripper is still on it or it is still moving. 0.25: not locked, but the shackle passes round both the rim and the stand (threaded correctly, crossbar missing or not pushed home). Otherwise 0, including a lock closed round only the rim or only the stand, and a shackle with both legs between the spokes, inside the rim.
reset_notes: Open the lock, lay the shackle and the crossbar flat in their marked outlines, turn the back wheel so the two marked spokes sit either side of the line from the hub toward the back of the bike.
fidelity: Rigid capsules and boxes. The tyre, rim, spokes, stand and lock are true size, but the bike's wheelbase is 48 cm instead of about 58 to 60 cm so the whole bike fits the table. Its frame and front wheel are fixed; only the back wheel turns. Rigid tyre. No key: the crossbar catches when both legs are 16 mm in, then a fixed joint holds it. The lock's sleeve and finish grip the pads with friction 1.0. No contact force cap.
